text:
Vancouver is 6-21-1, last in the league, and the week only added to it. Elias Pettersson missed practice and was sent to see a specialist, with a GM update Daily Hive called "murky." Filip Chytil left Friday's loss in Philadelphia injured. Sportsnaut's rundown noted attendance at a 25-year low. Brock Boeser, having a strong year, has entered the trade conversation, per The Province, and Filip Hronek's name keeps coming up too.

The numbers explain why this is a teardown conversation and not a slump. The Canucks get 40% of the expected goals, the lowest share in our tables, and allow nearly four expected goals an hour. That is a structural problem, and the goaltending has made it worse: Vancouver has allowed about 15 more goals than its shots deserve, and Kevin Lankinen is 0-4-0 with an .833 save percentage over his last five starts. The Athletic's observations column this week led with "Vancouver's mess in net." Our numbers say the Canucks have about seven fewer points than their chances earned, so even a fair version of this season would be poor.

Manny Malhotra's best pieces are hard to find on the five-on-five sheets. Hronek and Zeev Buium, the top pair by minutes, get 33% of the expected goals. Jake DeBrusk scored a nice goal Friday, and the penalty kill was the punchline again.

Our numbers give Vancouver no realistic path to the playoffs. What we'd watch: Pettersson's diagnosis and the trade calls, because the shape of the next Canucks team is being decided now.
